title: eFAST & the RUSH Exam
keywords: 6 views RUQ subxiphoid LUQ pelvis right lung left lung
negative eFAST does not exclude solid organ injury
sources: Critical Vector — EM Pocket Guide: eFAST (ACEP 2023)
ACEP ultrasound guidelines; Perera P et al. RUSH exam

changelog.change: Initial entry — the 6 eFAST views + positive-exam actions, and the RUSH pump/tank/pipes framework with the shock-pattern table and IVC interpretation.

summary: eFAST answers one question fast: is there free fluid (peritoneal, pericardial, pleural) or a pneumothorax? A positive eFAST in an unstable patient goes to the operating room, not the CT scanner. A negative eFAST does NOT exclude solid-organ injury — CT remains standard for the stable patient with a concerning mechanism.

rows: Right mid-axillary line, ~10th ICS; also fan above the diaphragm
Probe flat, aimed at the left shoulder
Posterior mid-axillary line, 8th–9th ICS; fan above the diaphragm
Free fluid; haemothorax (harder view than RUQ)
Sagittal + transverse, bladder as the window
Free fluid in the rectovesical pouch (♂) or pouch of Douglas (♀)
Lung sliding vs barcode sign (M-mode: seashore = sliding, barcode = pneumothorax)
As above — always bilateral for pneumothorax

body.text: Sensitivity for free fluid ~ 75–88%; for pneumothorax ~ 49–99% (operator- and study-dependent). A lung point (the transition between sliding and no sliding) is 100% specific for pneumothorax; absent sliding alone is not.

rows: Emergent laparotomy — do not delay for CT; activate trauma surgery
CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast to characterise the injury
Pericardiocentesis (US-guided) as a bridge to the operating room / thoracotomy
Needle decompression / finger thoracostomy, then a chest tube

items: PUMP: parasternal/subxiphoid — eyeball LVEF, RV:LV ratio (> 1 = strain), pericardial effusion.
TANK: IVC + lungs — collapsed IVC = empty tank (hypovolaemia); plethoric IVC = full (cardiogenic / obstructive); bilateral B-lines = wet.
PIPES: aorta (measure for AAA) + femoral/popliteal compression for DVT.

rows: Elevated RAP / hypervolaemia — unlikely to respond

body.text: Mechanical ventilation, high PEEP, and raised intra-abdominal pressure all reduce the reliability of IVC collapsibility — use it with the clinical picture and a passive leg raise / fluid challenge, not alone.
